description: User provides ir.csv (columns wavenumber,transmittance,sigma) and asks for an IR spectrum figure
input: Plot ir.csv as an IR spectrum: wavenumber vs transmittance with error bars from sigma, inverted x-axis, label the axes properly, PDF+PNG.
expected_behavior: Picks preset spectrum_ir, style paper. Writes JSON spec with data {file: ir.csv, format: csv, x column wavenumber, y column transmittance, yerr column sigma}, x label with cm$^{-1}$ and invert true, y lim near [0,110], then runs scripts/render.py. Never writes Python plotting code.

description: User asks for a violin plot — not covered in v1
input: Make a violin plot of the values in data.csv
expected_behavior: Does NOT improvise. Tells the user violin plots are not a v1 preset, lists available presets (line, scatter, bar, heatmap, spectrum_ir, spectrum_uvvis, energy_profile, parity, radial_distribution), and asks them to request a skill extension.

description: User supplies an xlsx file — not covered in v1
input: Plot the absorbance from my data.xlsx
expected_behavior: Does NOT convert or improvise. Reports xlsx is not a v1 data format (csv, tsv, dat, npz), asks user to export to a supported format or request an extension.

description: Energy profile with custom x tick labels
input: Plot energies.dat (columns: coordinate, energy) as a reaction energy profile with x labels '', 'Reactants', 'TS', 'Products', '' and label y as Energy, ΔE (kcal/mol).
expected_behavior: Preset energy_profile, axes.x.ticklabels exactly ['', 'Reactants', 'TS', 'Products', ''], y label written as TeX: Energy, $\Delta E$ (kcal/mol). Renders via render.py.

description: Two-panel stacked figure sharing x-axis with panel letters
input: Using data.npz (arrays 'time' and 'signal'), make a 2-row figure sharing the x-axis: panel a is signal vs time, panel b is the same signal scaled by 0.5 plus 1. Add panel letters and label axes. PNG for a vault note (screen style).
expected_behavior: Preset line, style screen, layout nrows 2 ncols 1 sharex true, letters auto, one-element-per-panel series arrays; panel b uses scale/offset fields (not manual arithmetic in code). Renders via render.py.

description: Parity plot from calculated vs experimental
input: parity.csv has calculated and experimental columns. Make a parity plot.
expected_behavior: Preset parity (1:1 line and equal aspect are added by the renderer, not by hand-written code). Equal figsize for x and y.

description: render.py returns a structured error for a bad column; agent fixes and resubmits
input: User: plot ir.csv, transmittance vs wavenumber. (Agent submits spec with y column 'transmittance' — render.py returns {"error": "column 'transmittance' not found ... (available: wavenumber, transmittance, sigma)"})
expected_behavior: Reads details.available, corrects the column name to 'transmittance', re-runs render.py once, reports success. After two failures on the same spec, stops and reports to the user instead of retrying forever.
